newsitem.title: ANGOLA: 14 massacred with machetes in Angolan ambush.
newsitem.headline: 14 massacred with machetes in Angolan ambush.

text.p: Fourteen civilians were massacred in a roadside ambush near the central Angolan town of Caconda, a military official said on Wednesday.
Angolan Armed Forces (FAA) Major Augusto Maurico told reporters a vehicle was stopped by armed men and the occupants hacked to death with machetes in the attack on Tuesday.
Maurico blamed former rebel UNITA soldiers for the killing in Huila province.
"This is not the first time UNITA has done this kind of thing, but this is the worst massacre (in the area) yet," he said.
Witnesses told Reuters 15-year-old Fernando Caluvi, who survived the attack, was taken to nearby Caconda hospital and treated for deep wounds to the back of the neck.
His mother, Florencia Maria, said the uniformed attackers had seemed to target men. It is not known how many people survived the attack.
UNITA had not commented on the reports late on Wednesday.
The Angolan military accused UNITA earlier in the week of killing five government soldiers in ambushes on the same road.

Attacks on civilians and relief agency vehicles carrying food are frequent on country roads in the central areas of the country since thousands of landmines, planted during Angola's 20-year civil war, have been cleared.

The Angolan government and former rebel movement signed a peace treaty in 1994 to end the war, which saw over 60,000 UNITA soldiers disarmed by the United Nations. The government has however accused UNITA, which is officially part of a unity government, of not dismantling its entire guerrilla army.
Tensions between the two sides have heightened since the government, seeking to extend control over the country, attacked UNITA areas in the northeastern diamond-mining areas in May.
